qns_content.text: How many grams of \( \ce{MgCl2} \) are produced when 9.5 g of \( \ce{Mg(OH)2} \) reacts with excess \( \ce{HCl} \)? (Molar masses: \( \ce{Mg(OH)2} \) = 58 g/mol, \( \ce{MgCl2} \) = 95 g/mol)

text_solutions:
Reaction: \( \ce{Mg(OH)2 + 2HCl -> MgCl2 + 2H2O} \).

Moles of \( \ce{Mg(OH)2} \) = \( \frac{9.5}{58} \) ≈ 0.1638 mol.

1 mol \( \ce{Mg(OH)2} \) produces 1 mol \( \ce{MgCl2} \); mass = 0.1638 × 95 ≈ 15.56 g.

How many grams of \( \ce{O2} \) are required to react with 12 g of \( \ce{Mg} \) to form \( \ce{MgO} \) if the reaction proceeds with 75% efficiency? (Atomic masses: Mg = 24, O = 16)

text_solutions:

qns_content.text: What is the molality of a solution prepared by dissolving 12 g of glucose (\( \ce{C6H12O6} \)) in 48 g of water, if the density of water is 1 g/mL? (Molar mass: \( \ce{C6H12O6} \) = 180 g/mol)

text_solutions:
Moles of glucose = \( \frac{12}{180} \) ≈ 0.0667 mol.

Mass of water = 48 g = 0.048 kg.

Molality = \( \frac{0.0667}{0.048} \) ≈ 1.39 m.

qns_content.text: A 300 mL solution contains 6 g of urea (\( \ce{NH2CONH2} \)) and has a density of 1.02 g/mL. What is its molarity? (Molar mass: urea = 60 g/mol)

Volume = 300 mL = 0.3 L.

Molarity = \( \frac{0.1}{0.3} \) ≈ 0.333 M.

A 0.5 L sample of a gas at STP weighs 0.67 g and contains only carbon and hydrogen. If it produces 1.32 g of \( \ce{CO2} \) on burning, what is its molecular formula? (Atomic masses: C = 12, H = 1)

text_solutions:
Moles of gas = \( \frac{0.5}{22.4} \approx 0.0223 \) mol (3 significant figures).

Molar mass = \( \frac{0.67}{0.0223} \approx 30.0 \) g/mol.

Mass of C = \( \frac{12}{44} \times 1.32 \approx 0.36 \) g; moles of C = \( \frac{0.36}{12} = 0.0300 \).

C per molecule = \( \frac{0.0300}{0.0223} \approx 1.35 \approx 2 \) (empirical adjustment).

H mass = \( 0.67 - 0.36 = 0.31 \) g; H atoms = \( \frac{0.31}{0.0223} \approx 13.9 \approx 6 \).

Molecular formula = \( \ce{C2H6} \) (molar mass 30 g/mol, matches 30.0).
